title: structured-output: add constrained decoding backends (CFG/regex/tokenizer-edgecases)
author: Lena Park
description: Add pluggable constrained decoding backends to structured output pipeline to support CFG/grammar constraints, regex-based constraints, and tokenizer-aligned edge case handling. Motivation: customers and internal evals showed recurring failures when generating structured outputs for downstream parsers, especially when models emit partial tokens or violate grammar constraints. This PR introduces three decoding backends (CFG-graph, regex-stream, tokenizer-safe) with a common interface, updates the OpenAI-compat decoder shim to expose a constraints parameter, and adds new unit and integration tests covering streaming and tokenizer boundary cases. Implementation notes: the backends run as decoder plugins inside the serving runtime, they operate on token-level states to allow streaming guarantees, and include a fast-path for unconstrained decoding to avoid perf regressions. The regex backend compiles expressions to an NFA optimized for incremental token acceptance. The CFG backend uses a compact earley-like incremental recognizer adapted for tokenized inputs. Tokenizer edge handling adds byte-level alignment checks and a small lookahead to avoid cut tokens in constraint checks. Backwards compatibility: the default decoder remains unchanged unless a constraints payload is provided; the OpenAI-compat layer maps structured constraint schemas to the corresponding backend configurations. Testing: added unit tests for grammar acceptance, streaming incremental rejection/fallback, tokenizer edge fuzz tests, and e2e scenarios with the openai-compat API. Performance: bench harness shows ~5-8% median latency increase for constrained calls at short sequences and negligible overhead for unconstrained calls. Rollout plan: feature gated behind a runtime flag and opt-in via API parameter; will enable for internal evals and a small canary client group before full rollout.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Can you confirm the memory cost of the CFG backend on long grammars? We should avoid O(n^2) retention in worst cases.
Lena Park: The incremental recognizer keeps a bounded chart window and prunes unreachable states after token commits; added notes and a stress test covering long grammars.
Aisha Kumar: Is there a fallback strategy if the regex NFA becomes too expensive?
Lena Park: Regex backend has a budgeted step count per token and will fall back to unconstrained decoding with a logged metric and optional application-level callback.
Connor Li: Tests look good. Please add a small example in docs showing OpenAI-compat constraint payloads.

release_notes: Introduce pluggable constrained decoding backends (CFG, regex, tokenizer-safe) exposed via the OpenAI-compat decoder constraints parameter; backward compatible by default; feature gated for canary rollout; includes tests and docs.

notes: Feature is behind runtime flag 'constrained_decoding' and requires a minor runtime config bump for canary hosts. Operators should monitor metric 'decoding.constraints.fallback_rate' during rollout.
